openQuestions.text: What does the hook brief actually put in front of a model today, and can a model on each of the six CLIs act on it without guessing the command id, its policy, the document to read and whether it was already offered?
Which command-discovery surface defects (the g5 `skill.md` collision and its siblings) keep a command from being offered or found on each runtime, and what detects them before a user hits one?

resolvedQuestions.text: Where does the ~205 ms Claude hook wall time go, and which part can be removed without changing the recommendation?
Which hook or pointer surface must each of the six runtimes have before an advisor recommendation is even offered, and which runtimes are unwired in the pre-arm log?
What does command surfacing cost in tokens per prompt, per session and per started command, and where is the largest avoidable cost?

Which before-arm runtime behaviour explains the start rates (claude 3 of 12, codex 0 of 12, pi 0 of 12, devin 2 of 12 or 12, opencode 4 of 9, dsh 3 of 8), and what stops a model from starting an offered command?
Why does the model start so few offered commands on each runtime (claude 3/12, codex 0/12, pi 0/12, devin 2/11, opencode 3/7, dsh 2/7), and what does the missing COMMAND line prove about the brief?
Which change to the brief contract or hook wiring raises start rate per runtime, and how does it extend rather than duplicate planned phases 005-008?
Which cold-start paths (daemon, embedder, first prompt of a session) can exceed the runtime's hook budget, and what removes the stall?
How must command files be laid out and installed so a fresh external repository exposes every command on every runtime, given the g5 skill.md folder-shadowing result?
What does a person installing Skilled into an external repository see on first run, and where does the setup path still fail silently after the embedder work phase 008 plans?
Which caching or precompute change pays for itself across the six CLIs, and which does not?
What is the cheapest reliable way to measure start rate across six runtimes without running pi, ollama, or the full test suite?
What is the measured cost of the brief and of the hook (latency, tokens, cold start, embedder), and which part of that cost is invisible to the person paying it?
Which per-runtime architecture spends the least per prompt, and what should the other runtimes copy?

keyFindings.text: **The brief is a 3-line, 240-296 character payload (about 60-74 tokens at 4 chars per token), and most of it is prompt-independent.** Probes 1 to 6 measured 258 to 296 characters; the greeting probe measured 240 characters with `Advisor: prompt skipped.` as its head. The static `Directives:` block plus the comment-hygiene line is 233 characters of every payload, so 79 to 90 percent of a short brief is identical on every prompt. keyFindings.text: The Claude prompt path starts three Node processes per prompt before any scoring: the `bash -c` wrapper starts the spec-kit shim, the shim `spawnSync`s the advisor hook, and the advisor hook spawns `.skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs`. One bare `node -e 0` start measured 36.85 ms median (min 22.90, max 47.31, n=15) on the same machine that recorded a 205.09 ms hook median. Three starts therefore account for roughly 100 to 110 ms of that median, before any hook or scorer work. keyFindings.text: **The pre-arm start rate is not a surfacing baseline.** Phase 005 is planned, not built, so no brief in the pre-arm names a command; `started` is defined as a read of the expected command document *or* a `COMMAND:` line, not as a response to a brief. The 3/12, 0/12, and similar numbers therefore measure spontaneous document reads, not whether a model starts an offered command. One of those three processes is removable without touching scoring: the hook could speak the existing JSON-RPC to the daemon in-process through the launcher bridge it already locates, instead of spawning the CLI. The CLI remains the cold-start launcher and the local-scorer fallback. The expected saving is the measured process start plus the CLI's argument and schema work, so the 205.09 ms median should land near 165 to 170 ms. The exact files are `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/skill-advisor-cli-fallback.ts` (add a direct bridge path beside `runCliRecommend`) and `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts` (keep the CLI entry for cold start and fallback). keyFindings.text: The cold-start caps on the two sides of the shim disagree, and the tighter one wins. The shim passes the advisor child a 2200 ms budget (`CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS` 2500 minus a 300 ms start margin) and kills it at 2500 ms, while the CLI may wait up to 5000 ms for a cold daemon before its local fallback answers. A daemon cold start between 2.2 s and 5 s therefore produces a fail-open prompt even though the CLI was still working correctly. A recorded sandbox run already shows the failure shape at 2508 ms. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.js:137] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:34] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/host-integrations/003-pi-skill-orchestrator-based-research-refinement/011-observation-fixes/evidence/goal-reverify/reports/pi-433.md:1]

keyFindings.text: **Five runtimes have an in-repo delivery path; DSH is conditional and unconfigured here.** Claude runs the advisor through the spec-kit shim (2,500 ms budget), Codex and Devin through their own shims calling the same Claude adapter (2,800 ms), Pi through an auto-loaded extension that calls the compiled advisor in-process, and OpenCode through its plugin. DSH's `prompt-advisor` adapter returns immediately unless `options.promptAdvisor === true`, and no repo-side DSH config enables that flag. The cheapest fix for finding 3 is not a bigger timeout: it is moving the cold daemon start off the prompt path. A Claude `SessionStart` group already exists with eight adapters, and none of them warms the advisor. Adding one detached `advisor_status --warm-only` call there should cost the session about 65 ms once, and remove the first-prompt cold penalty entirely. The exact files are `.claude/settings.json` (one detached SessionStart command) and, for the other runtimes, the equivalent session-start surface in `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md` section 2. The measurable gain is the first-prompt p95 moving from the 2500 ms timeout ceiling to the warm ~205 ms, with zero first-prompt `fail_open` outage briefs. keyFindings.text: **The harness cannot see an offer.** The hook diagnostic record is a closed, prompt-free schema with `skillLabel`, `emittedBytes` and `directivesSuppressed`, and no field for the command or its policy. `skillLabelFor` returns the metadata label or the top recommendation's skill id, so even a command-bearing brief records only its skill. The only offer evidence today is the model's own `COMMAND:` narration, which was 0 of 24 on five runtimes and 1 of 8 on dsh in the before arm. keyFindings.text: **A doctor sub-route's start can never be scored from its document read.** `commandParts('/doctor:git hooks')` keeps `git hooks` as the name, and `documentTails` then looks for `/commands/doctor/git hooks.md`, which cannot exist. Reproduced with a synthetic read of `.skilled/commands/doctor/git.md`: `startState` says `started: false` for `/doctor:git hooks` and `started: true` for `/doctor:git`. 28 of the 35 doctor command strings in the renderer carry an argument. The current behaviour corpus uses base commands, so the before arm is unaffected; any future doctor row or a model that prints the argued string is affected. Phase 006 adds a "Starting a surfaced command" table and tells the model to read the command document, which covers the intended path, but no phase maps the canonical label to the host entry or measures an attempted host invocation that fails. keyFindings.text: **The G5 shadowing defect is documented by phase 006 but fixed by no phase.** `.claude/commands/create/skill.md` is a symlink to the canonical command file; with a `skill.md` present Claude Code lists the whole folder as one Skill entry named `create` and hides the other twelve `create:*` names. Phase 006's T018 writes that fact into the hook doc and stops there. **G5's blast radius is exactly one namespace and twelve commands.** Only `create` carries a lowercase `skill.md` under `.skilled/commands`; its mirror is a folder-preserving symlink at `.claude/commands/create/skill.md` created by `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs`. The folder holds 12 sibling commands, so the shadow costs all 12 Claude names, not one. **The aggregate start rate hides a policy split that inverts per runtime.** Claude's 3 of 12 is **3 of 4 read-only `run` rows and 0 of 8 mutating `start` rows**; opencode's 5 of 12 is 3 of 8 `start` and 2 of 4 `run`; dsh's 4 of 12 is 3 of 8 `start` and 1 of 4 `run`; codex is 0 of 8 and 0 of 4. The same number therefore describes opposite behaviour: claude adopts only checks it cannot improvise, while opencode and dsh adopt creation workflows. keyFindings.text: The Ollama adapter never sends `keep_alive`, so the server's default 5-minute unload applies. The measured file confirms it: at 21:25:08 the loaded model's `expires_at` was 21:29:57, four minutes and 49 seconds later. After that gap the next prompt pays a cold embed of 271 to 277 ms against a 6.57 ms warm median, roughly a 40x tax on that call. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/embeddings/adapters/ollama.ts:343] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/008-embedder-setup-and-cost/scratch/measured-2026-11-12.txt:12] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/008-embedder-setup-and-cost/scratch/measured-2026-11-12.txt:36]

The cold embed is a latency tax, not a fail-open. Phase 008 plans a 750 ms prompt deadline, and a 271 to 277 ms cold call fits it with about 475 ms of headroom, so the prompt still gets its cosine. What the person pays is one slower prompt after every idle gap, not a lost recommendation. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/008-embedder-setup-and-cost/spec.md:130] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/008-embedder-setup-and-cost/spec.md:174]

**The G5 experiment does not prove the defect on the real mirror path.** Its listing mixes built-in skills (`dataviz`, `init`, `security-review`) with the `create` entries, so the tested folder behaved as a skill folder; whether `.claude/commands/create/skill.md` shadows the same 12 names is not established by the artifact. The cheap decisive test is one throwaway repo with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)` and two listings, with and without the basename. Reproduce before changing layout. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/007-per-runtime-behaviour-proof/scratch/g5/listing-a.txt:1] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/007-per-runtime-behaviour-proof/scratch/g5/listing-b.txt:1]

**The start rate measures the path, not the outcome.** Devin's two `/create:agent` runs wrote `.skilled/agents/dependency-audit.md`, `.claude/agents/dependency-audit.md` and `.devin/agents/dependency-audit/` — the exact artifacts the command exists to produce — yet score `started: false` because they never read the document. The same holds for `/create:command` writing `.skilled/skills/prompt-shortcut/`: 5 of devin's 8 mutating rows wrote, while 0 of 8 scored started. A run that does the work its own way and a run that does nothing are indistinguishable in the headline number, and the declared "write target per command" from phase 002 is prose in `gate3_location` ("a new or updated OpenCode skill package at --path"), not a path prefix any check can match. keyFindings.text: **Codex's pre-arm is missing its brief for a harness reason, not a model reason.** The repo turns hooks on, but Codex runs a project hook only after the exact entry is approved and stored as `trusted_hash` in `~/.codex/config.toml`; the arena paths under `/private/var/folders/.../skilled-behaviour-arenas/` have no project entry there. The runner passes no `CODEX_HOME` and no trust setting. Six of six raw Codex transcripts contain no `Advisor:` line, so Codex's 0/12 measures a session with no advisor, and it cannot be compared with a runtime that got one. keyFindings.text: Phase 008's deadline should be passed into the adapter, not raced around it. The adapter already builds an `AbortController` per request and takes an instance `timeoutMs`, but the advisor's registry shim re-exports a `getAdapter(name)` factory with no options, so today the wrapper can only abandon a 5000 ms request. Adding an options argument to the shared `getAdapter` and constructing the prompt-time adapter with `timeoutMs: 750` makes the abort real and frees the socket for the next prompt. This refines 008's planned wrapper deadline rather than repeating it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/embeddings/adapters/ollama.ts:129] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/embeddings/adapters/ollama.ts:137] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/embeddings/registry.ts:83] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/embedders/registry.ts:17]

**The scorer cannot see the brief on the runtimes that inject it out of band.** The raw Claude transcripts contain `Advisor:` in 6 of 6 sampled sessions, while the normalized records the scorer reads contain it in 0 of 6; Pi's in-prompt injection is visible in 6 of 6, and OpenCode's hook context in 1 of 6. So a `started` fact is attributable to the brief on no runtime, and a `declined` judgment is unsupported everywhere. A start rate can move for reasons other than surfacing and the current summary would not show it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/score-command-transcripts.mjs:325] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/score-command-transcripts.mjs:646]

The 30.6 ms p95 tail is not the cold model. A cold call costs 271 to 277 ms, so even three cold calls inside a 44-prompt set would push p95 to roughly 470 ms, not the observed 262 ms. The tail is steady-state variance around a 6.57 ms median embed, bounded at tens of milliseconds, and the 100 to 110 ms process-start share from iteration 1 is five times larger.
